newsitem.title: USA: Burger King agrees to make restaurants accessible.
newsitem.headline: Burger King agrees to make restaurants accessible.

text.p: Hamburger chain Burger King Corp, owned by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc Tuesday agreed to survey all its company-owned restaurants and remove any barriers to accessibility which violate the Americans with Disabilities Act.
The agreement settles a lawsuit brought on behalf of disabled citizens, according to the Disability Rights Council of Greater Washington, a co-plaintiff in the litigation.

Co-plaintiff Patricia Day, a self-described "junk food junkie", initiated the lawsuit after her wheelchair began entangled in the metal barriers of a food queue at a brand-new Burger King restaurant near her home in Bowie, Maryland.
Several people had to help extricate Day and her wheelchair in the incident, which she descibed as "humilitating."
"Now that this settlment has been reached, I can look forward to going through the line with my husband and daughter, just like any other family," she said in a statement.

Under the agreement, Burger King committed to taking action to resolve any access problems identified in the survey in order to assure that their company-owned restaurants were in full compliance with the ADA, a federal law passed in 1992 to ensure that people with disabilities have equal access to public buildings.

"We are pleased that Burger King Corporation has agreed to undertake this major effort to identify and resolve any barriers that may prevent people with disabilities from going to their restaurants," said Julia Bell, executive director of the Disability Rights Council.
The chain has also taken action to assure that architectural plans for future restaurants provide full access for individuals with disabilities.

"We recognize the important of assuring that all of our customers are able to enjoy their experience at any of our restaurants, and are committed to taking the necessary steps to achieve that goal," David Fitzjohn, senior vice president for worldwide development at Burger King, said in a statement.
